evidence: Cic. Fin. 5.35: tōtaque figūra et fōrma et statūra (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The shape of anything; of a person also beauty (fōrmā excellente, Liv. 1.9.11, Lewis & Short). A mould is a fōrma too (see baking tin).

terms.gloss: figure, shape; the form of a word
terms.comment: From fingō, mould: the outline a thing has been given. In grammar the form of a word (Traupman 318; M-O s.v. form, grammatical).

phrases.latin: nūdaque cōnsistunt, fōrmam servantia testae, vīna
phrases.english: the wine stands bare, keeping the shape of its jar

phrases.latin: Figūra est aut simplex, ut “doctus,” aut composita, ut “indoctus.”
phrases.english: The form is either simple, like “doctus,” or compound, like “indoctus.”
Form the imperative of the verb “venīre”.

forma.html: De Vaan 233–234, s.v. fōrma, prints the o long; Ernout–Meillet “stress the length of o”, which he takes for a recent lengthening of short o before r and a consonant (Leumann 1977: 114).
